rationale_evidence.anchor: Why policy version matters ... 2026 Threshold=0.90 means accepted. In 2027 Threshold=0.95. The same evidence may produce different conclusions under the two policies. Therefore we must preserve PolicyVersion with the assessment/conclusion. Otherwise historical reconstruction becomes ambiguous.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues policy version must be preserved with every assessment/conclusion, since a threshold change (e.g. 0.90→0.95) makes the same evidence yield different conclusions across time, and omitting it makes historical reconstruction ambiguous.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Why ontology version matters ... SecurityStatus changes. Then an old conclusion may not be interpretable under the new semantic model. Therefore SemanticModelVersion or equivalent provenance is necessary. This is especially important for KnowledgeOS because the ontology itself may evolve.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues a SemanticModelVersion (or equivalent provenance) must also be preserved, since changes to a concept's meaning (e.g. SecurityStatus) can make old conclusions uninterpretable under a newer ontology.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Retraction and belief revision ... A_1:P is accepted. Later e_2:\neg P. If we simply remove P, we lose history. rationale_evidence.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS needs belief-revision semantics rather than either deleting a contradicted assertion or keeping both as current truths, defining a six-value Status(A) enum {Active,Superseded,Retracted,Expired,Contested,Historical}.
